objective: Compute each numeric key once and stably sort opaque original values without native undefined-value special handling.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Sorting records by a selected value is practical.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Decorate-sort-undecorate separates key extraction and comparison.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Dense bounded opaque inputs clarify reference ownership.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Raw undefined sorting and inconsistent callback evaluation cause subtle defects.

defects: Raw-value native sort always moved undefined last without using pick, unlike senior decoration.
Boards disagreed on whether pick ran once or multiple times.
Input ownership, callback arguments/order/errors, freshness and sort cost model were implicit.
rationale: Decorate original items with numeric keys and indices before sorting in reference/junior, preserving the correct senior approach. Align skeleton/hint/approach to wrappers so opaque undefined can be sorted by its picked key. Define one ordered single-argument pick per input, bounded finite keys, original reference/value preservation, unchanged frozen input and fresh output. Explain n log n as the comparison-sort model excluding pick, not an ECMAScript native-sort guarantee. Add undefined before object keys, NaN/signed-zero original values, exact key-call protocol, original thrown value, cross-call freshness and 10000 stable tied records.

objective: Apply only own string-keyed changes as safe data properties with strict inequality and synchronous post-store notifications.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Object updates and callback notifications remain current.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Own-key boundaries, strict comparison and write-before-notify transfer widely.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Mutable own data settings and read-only changes scope the lesson.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Inherited keys and __proto__ setters are material correctness/security risks.

defects: All boards traversed inherited changes and assigned __proto__ through its inherited setter.
Missing own settings values could be mistaken for prototype properties.
NaN/zero identity, callback errors and notification ordering were implicit.
rationale: Guard Object.hasOwn(changes,key), read only own settings values and write changed values with own writable/enumerable/configurable data descriptors in every board. Update skeleton/hint/approach. Define normal key order, skip inherited/nonenumerable/symbol keys, preserve prototype and opaque references, do not add an absent undefined key, keep !== semantics (NaN changes, signed zeros do not). Notify synchronously with exactly key/old/new after storing; original throw stops with prior writes retained. Add own __proto__/constructor, inherited/symbol/hidden exclusion, exact notification/store order, original identities/errors and 10000 applied keys.

objective: Chain independent timeout callbacks from a positive count down to one with no inline tick and bounded simultaneous state.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Finite repeated work illustrates timer lifecycle.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Deferred recursion and constant simultaneous state transfer widely.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Bounded integer counts/delays and normal-return callbacks isolate the exercise.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Inline execution, missing termination and shared counters are common errors.

defects: Count/delay bounds and exact callback protocol were implicit.
Timer waiting was not separated from algorithmic dispatch work.
A ten-tick cap passed the old five-tick maximum.
rationale: Retain all correct timeout-chain forms. Define from 0..1000, positive bounded delay, exact one-argument normally-returning callback, ignored returns, independent sequences and only the next tick scheduled. Explain linear complete dispatch count and constant simultaneously retained state excluding host/wait/callback cost, without exact wall-clock claims. Add a 100-tick sequence within native VM wait limits with sum/last/arity/no-inline observations and two overlapping independent countdowns. The supported 1000 bound is source-reviewed rather than claimed as a maximum native timing run.

objective: Register one delayed reminder per future event with captured original title/delay and unchanged input.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Timer registration over event lists remains current.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Capture-time values and relative delays transfer to async code.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Bounded future delay avoids host overflow and excessive waits.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Mutation after registration and truncating the list can lose reminders.

defects: Junior read event.title when the timer fired, unlike reference/senior capture at registration.
Readonly ownership, timestamp/delay bounds, duplicate/tie behavior and callback arity were implicit.
A ten-event cap passed old small lists.
rationale: Capture title before the junior timeout callback and align the approach. Define at most 1000 read-only dense records, bounded string titles/nonnegative timestamps, future delay 1..1000, capture-time title/delay, independent duplicate timers, same-delay input order, no input mutation and exact one-argument normal callbacks. Separate linear registration/retained timer data from waiting/host/user callback cost. Add caller mutation/truncation after registration, duplicate equal-time delivery, 1000 past records and a last-position future event after 999 skipped records.
